thread:
maria: Hi team — customer ACME reports embeddings calls suddenly returning 403 while generations still work. They switched to Azure AD last week. Can we triage?

sam: Can you paste one failing request (redact keys)? quick curl or header is fine.

maria: Here — they said this is minimal repro:

```
POST /v1/embeddings
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted-jwt>
Content-Type: application/json

{ \"model\": \"embed-large-v2\", \"input\": \"hello\" }
```

Response: 403 { \"error\": \"missing_scope: embeddings.write\" }

jessica: important detail: their IDP issues the scope claim under `roles_uri` (custom namespaced claim) instead of the standard `scope`/`scp`. our authz layer only checks `scp` and `scope`.

arjun: ugh. do we have an example JWT from them? maria: provided a sanitized claims payload:

```
{
  \"iss\": \"https://sts.windows.net/...,\",
  \"aud\": \"api.redwood\",
  \"roles_uri\": \"https://acme.example.com/claims/scopes\",
  \"roles\": [\"inference:generate\",\"r:read\"]
}
```

sam: So embeddings permission exists but under a namespaced claim + roles array with slightly different strings. our matcher fails -> 403. That explains why gen works (they used a fallback service key) but embeddings do not.

arjun: quick workaround: create a tenant-scoped service key (from console) for ACME and attach explicit embeddings/rerank perms, then ask them to switch to that key. That buys time.

maria: customer asked for a permanent fix — will need to accept namespaced claims. Any objections to updating authz to accept `roles`, `roles_uri` and `scp`?

jessica: we should be careful. accepting arbitrary namespaced claims can be risky. propose: update mapping to check these in this order: 1) scope/s, 2) scp, 3) common namespaced claim URIs if present. Only accept exact allowed strings (embeddings.*, inference.*).

sam: agree. Also add a small middleware to normalize claims into a canonical `scopes` array for downstream checks.

arjun: can we patch prod quickly? small change in auth-proxy (5 LOC) + unit tests. We can rollout as a canary to customer tenant first.

maria: steps I will take: 1) create tenant-scoped service key and share with ACME (temp fix) 2) open infra ticket to patch auth-proxy and add acceptance tests 3) schedule canary against ACME tenant 4) monitor logs for false positives.

infra-bot: deploy-ticket created: INF-4921 — auth-proxy: normalize namespaced claims -> scp. Link: https://infra.redwood/internal/tickets/INF-4921

jessica: I'll add unit tests for the claim normalization and a small integration test using a mocked JWT with `roles_uri` payload.

support-bot: escalation notes: ACME case #41234 — root cause: Azure AD claim namespace mismatch. Impact: embeddings and rerank return 403; generation unaffected with fallback service key.

maria: customer confirmed they can use the temporary service key for now. Requested ETA for full fix?

arjun: estimate: patch + tests + canary = ~48 hours if nothing blocks. If we need a quick hotpatch without full test coverage we can do ~6 hours but I'd rather not.

jessica: I'll prioritize tests and try to get a reviewed PR within 8 hours.

maria: perfect — please ping me when PR is up and I'll update ACME. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: long-term: add IDP onboarding checklist to runbook to include claim namespaces and a script to validate token claims before provisioning. https://runbooks.redwood/internal/idp-onboarding#claim-checks

maria: noted. closing the triage thread once INF-4921 is scheduled.

support-bot: thread closed by maria at 1748888955
